title: Baoh
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Teenager Ikuro Hashizawa is abducted by a secret organization (Doress, called Judas in the Viz edition) and implanted with the Baoh parasite, which turns him into a near-unkillable mutant when threatened (AniList; MangaUpdates; ANN column). A young psychic girl (Sumire, Violet in the Viz edition), about 10, frees him and they flee while the chief scientist sends ever-stronger assassins after them (ANN). Hirohiko Araki's 1984 two-volume shounen action story, his work before JoJo's Bizarre Adventure.
life_message: It holds up loyalty to a friend and refusing to become someone else's weapon as what makes a person human.

content.note: Melting, exploding and sliced heads, dismembered animals; 'blood-splattered, brainmatter-drenched' (ANN); AniList Gore; MangaUpdates Blood and Gore.
Human experiments and body horror (MangaUpdates Body Horror, Human Experiment/s); hunted fugitives.
No nudity or fan service (ANN). The young psychic girl has a non-sexual crush on the teenage hero.
Purple prose and sound effects (ANN); nothing coarse noted.
Amnesia; hero fears the beast within (ANN).

dominant: Friendship and protecting the weak, unethical science critiqued, monstrous power

frames.aligns: Human dignity against experiments on people; protecting a child.
Ikuro resists the beast within him.
frames.concerns: Gore and rage feed the passions.

frames.aligns: Good versus evil plain; no sexual content.
Self-sacrificing protection of an innocent girl.
Image of God violated by human experiments.
Clear moral framing of hero and villain.
Hero refuses to be a weapon for others.
frames.concerns: Violence is the whole climax of every chapter.

frames.aligns: Outsiders rejected by 'normal' people find friendship (ANN).
frames.concerns: Female characters mostly victims or fans (ANN).

frames.aligns: Protecting the weak; justice against oppressors.
Critique of unethical science and militarism.
frames.concerns: ANN calls it 'a bit sexist'; glorified violence.

frames.aligns: Worth of outsiders; consent violated by experiments.
Power used to protect, not harm the innocent.
Sincere bond between Ikuro and the girl.
Saving a life; experiments on humans condemned.
Human dignity against misuse of science.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Bond with a stranger child becomes chosen family.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Modern science-fiction world of labs and parasites.

folkways.japan: A 1980s Weekly Shonen Jump action story built on the Jump values of friendship, struggle and victory.

delivery.evidence: ANN: campy melodrama; volume 2 cover promises 'the true meaning of friendship!'

personified.ideology: science that turns people into weapons

delivery.note: Themes are carried by fights and the hero's bond with the girl rather than argued.

winners_losers: Ikuro defeats a chain of assassins; the organization's weapon program gets no sympathy. The ending is not described in the sources.
to_verify: Ending (AniList Tragedy and Time Skip spoiler tags).
Character names differ between the Viz edition (Violet, Hazyeye, Judas) and MangaUpdates (Sumire, Kasuminome, Doress).
MangaUpdates lists it as out of print in English.
